title: Sentinel Curator: phased apply and circuited throttles for safe prefetch & batch tuning
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Ship an automated, auditable control-plane component (Sentinel Curator) that proposes batching and KV-prefetch configuration deltas, applies them in phased windows, enforces circuited throttles, and performs automatic rollback on SLO anomalies. This reduces token/unit costs while preserving p50/p95 latency and error-rate SLOs for multi-tenant workloads.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: recommendation engine integration, staged apply controller (canary -> ramp -> full), limiter primitives (concurrency caps, token-buckets, micro-window rate fences), SLO-aware routing hooks, anomaly detection signals and rollback orchestration, safety dashboard and audit trail.
- Out-of-scope: model architecture changes, offline quantization pipeline, billing UI changes.

Design summary (high level):
1) Recommendation phase: offline and online advisor produce candidate config deltas (batch size, batching window, prefix-KV prefetch enable/size, model-variant mapping). Candidates are stored with metadata and expected cost delta and risk score.
2) Phased apply controller: staged rollout steps - dry-run (shadow apply), canary (1% of traffic or selected tenant cohort), progressive ramp with configurable step sizes, final steady-state. Each step has SLO gates.
3) Circuited limiters: enforce runtime guardrails during ramp - per-tenant concurrency cap, global in-flight token ceiling, per-route micro-window limiter. Limiters are configurable and can be temporarily tightened by the controller if anomalies surface.
4) SLO-aware routing: controller can redirect a small fraction of traffic to higher-SLO model variants or dedicated capacity automatically when latency risk is detected. Routing decisions are weighted and reversible.
5) Anomaly detection & rollback: multi-signal detector (p50/p95 latency, queue latency, error rate, model divergence score from eval set) triggers an automated rollback plan. Rollback is staged (stop ramp -> revert canary -> revert all) with post-mortem capture.
6) Observability & audit: per-change timeline, tokenized change ID, linked PR, acceptance metrics, and a dashboard for safety officers to pause/resume.

Acceptance criteria (must be met before merging to main):
- Controller can apply a sample candidate in dry-run mode with zero traffic impact.
- Canary apply at 1% traffic for a given route completes with SLO telemetry captured for p50/p95 and error rates.
- Automatic halt and rollback occur within 30s of a defined p95 latency breach of the SLO window (configurable threshold).
- Limiters successfully throttle without dropping requests in tests (no SLA violation).
- End-to-end e2e test coverage for canary->ramp->rollback flow and unit tests for limiter primitives.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: implement controller skeleton, limiter primitives, and shadow apply support.
- Week 2: integrate with recommendation API (mocked), implement canary step and telemetry plumbing.
- Week 3: implement anomaly detector, rollback sequence, and internal e2e.
- Week 4: safety review, experimentation with 2 internal customers, gradual opening.

Key metrics and dashboards to monitor during rollout:
- Cost delta (tokens/unit) per-route and per-tenant
- p50/p95 latency pre/post change, request queue latency, 5xx rate
- Failure/revert rate for applied candidates
- Time-to-detect and time-to-rollback for anomalies

Rollforward policy (when automatic rollback occurred and we want to reapply):
- Lock the candidate for manual review. Require 2 approvers (eng + product) and updated canary parameter (smaller step or reduced concurrency) before reattempt.

External integrations and links:
- PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/PRD-optimizations-sentinel-curator
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/designs/sentinel-curator.md
- GitHub draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3928
- Observability dashboard (alpha): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/optim/sentinel-curator-alpha

Security considerations:
- Candidate config changes must be signed and stored in audit log.
- Ensure no PII is exposed in telemetry snapshots retained by the controller.

Notes on trade-offs and alternatives considered:
- We considered a fully manual approval step between canary and ramp, but that increases time-to-cost-savings and reduces velocity. The phased automated approach with strict SLO gates provides a middle ground.
- Two limiter implementations evaluated: centralized (single service) vs. sidecar (per-runtime). We selected centralized primitives for operational visibility and easier cross-tenant coordination; plan to prototype sidecar later if latency shows impact.
